process_observations.observation: Both of the step's manifest members are named by a traceability row, and at --manifest-dir artefacts all fourteen rows resolve their artefact against a real component with 0 coverage gaps.

M1-S02 introduces no new RTM orphan: the Layout member form 'Case-Case Support Layout' is byte-identical to its file stem, so check_rtm.py's two index keys agree and the divergence that produced M1-S01's three orphans cannot occur for layouts.

The tester had already captured disk evidence for both halves of the manual test, including the per-layout field listings, so the UAT case was compiled from values a reviewer will actually read rather than from the test text restated.
Assumptions A13 and A26 both already list M1-S02 in their steps[], so this step needed no counterpart to M1-S01's W03 assumption-linkage gap.

Half of an answered blocking clarification is unbuilt and unbuildable from the cited skill: Q24 asks for the assignment-rule checkbox defaulted on, and the only element in the skill's inventory governs whether it is shown. Recorded as decisions.md D-M1S02-03 with the § 8 deepen-a-skill signal.

The step's checker acceptance test description predicts '0 finding(s)'; the checker prints 2, both INFO, and the declared expected 'exit 0' still holds. Reproduced in this run and recorded as planner open item O-M1S02-01.

The manual test's positional wording ('<layoutSections> is preceded by the assignment-rule checkbox') describes the inverse of the element order the cited skill's own example documents, so a reviewer ticking it literally would reject correct metadata. The presence reading was carried into the compiled case as its own step rather than silently adopted.

CWB-OTHER-005 is the second workbook row in this build whose verification cell names no test, for the same reason as CWB-OTHER-002: deploy-order.md is undeclared in outputs[] on both M1 steps. Recorded once as planner open item O-M1S02-02 rather than a third time per row.

check_workbook.py splits a table row on every bare pipe with no escape handling (L330), so an RTM-style escaped pipe inside a cell shifts every later column and the linter reads source_req_id as recommended_agent. The two new Section 2 rows were written with ';' and produce zero per-row findings; M1-S01's three rows in the Other configuration file keep the escaped pipe and are caught by nothing, because that heading is not a canonical section and the parser skips its rows entirely.

The layouts' field set is a builder default assembled from the skill's own example, M1-S01's compact layout and assumption A13; no clarification supplies a field list, and a reviewer expecting AccountId or ContactId on an account-centric intake page will find neither.
REQ-014's source is Q57, a deferred question, so the row rests on assumption A13 at risk medium rather than on an answer. REQ-010 is the only other row in the matrix in that position.

One manual test line covers two requirements with two different earliest verification dates, so TC-M1S02-01 is the first case in this build that is only partly tickable at its own gate. Compiled as one case per Step 10's rule, with the gap named in step 6's expected-result field.

The workbook row schema requires a named human as owner and explicitly not a team alias, but no source in this build names a person; the cells carry the clarification's owner_role with the substitution stated in the cell, unchanged from M1-S01.
Every step in milestone M1 is now documented, so the milestone's cross-step checks and acceptance report are due — including the record-type-to-layout assertion both step scopes left vacuous.
